chunks: Al-Saffar from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the expiation of a vow, so he said: The expiation of a vow is the expiation of an oath. And whoever vowed to sacrifice a she-camel, upon him is a camel which he should adorn and shear and stop with at Arafat. And whoever vowed to sacrifice a male camel, he may slaughter it wherever he wishes.

key_terms.النَّذْرُ: A vow, a promise to perform an act of worship or sacrifice
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation or compensation for a religious obligation or vow
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: A plain near Mecca, significant site for Hajj rituals
key_terms.يُقَلِّدُهَا: He adorns it (specifically with a bell or ornament)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking a vow to sacrifice an animal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain clarifies that the expiation for breaking a vow (kaffarat al-nadr) mirrors that of an oath (kaffarat al-yamin), establishing a unified legal principle in Shia jurisprudence. It specifically details the ritual for a camel vow, requiring the animal to be adorned, sheared, and presented at Arafat, while allowing flexibility for other sacrificial animals, reflecting the practical application of vows in early Islamic practice.
